units.rhetorical_move: says the currency has become indispensable

original_instantiations: the new currency has grown fast in recent years
it has become an indispensable part of the system

units.source_excerpt: Digital currency has developed rapidly and become an indispensable part of the system.
units.reusable_pattern: Open with a rapid rise and an indispensable status.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the indispensable.

units.rhetorical_move: calls the system brand-new

original_instantiations: the system is called brand-new
it rests on individual choice, national economy and international economy

units.source_excerpt: We construct a brand-new system from three perspectives.
units.reusable_pattern: Call a system brand-new and count its perspectives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth.

units.rhetorical_move: says either system achieves equilibrium if policies are proper
units.function: bind the result to a condition

original_instantiations: two exchange rate systems are compared
either reaches equilibrium if proper policies are implemented

units.source_excerpt: Either system would achieve equilibrium if proper policies are implemented.
units.reusable_pattern: Bind a result with if proper policies are implemented.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the condition.

units.rhetorical_move: says the finding is inspiring
units.function: let the result surprise the authors

original_instantiations: capital flows are added to the model
the finding is called inspiring

units.source_excerpt: It is inspiring that the new currency runs the economy more efficiently.
units.reusable_pattern: Preface a finding with it is inspiring that.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten the reaction.

units.rhetorical_move: proposes a bank affiliated with the United Nations

original_instantiations: stability needs shared rules
all accepting countries should co-create one affiliated bank

units.source_excerpt: We propose that all accepting countries co-create one affiliated bank.
units.reusable_pattern: Propose an institution with we propose and co-create.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the bank as already existing.

units.rhetorical_move: grants advantages, then names the precarious situation
units.function: turn with but in the meantime

original_instantiations: instant transactions and borderless transfer are granted
the value is then called precarious

units.source_excerpt: The form enables instant transactions, but in the meantime the value sits in a precarious situation.
units.reusable_pattern: Grant a benefit, then turn with but in the meantime.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the benefit.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model gives a clear overview
units.function: justify the model by what it enables

original_instantiations: modeling the mechanism is called necessary
the model gives a clear overview and helps make policies

units.source_excerpt: The model would enable a clear overview and help make policies.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a model by the overview it gives.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the model decides policy.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers the tasks with bullets

original_instantiations: seven tasks are set out as bullets
the last asks what happens if countries abandon their own currency

units.source_excerpt: The tasks are set out as bullets, and the last asks what abandonment would do.
units.reusable_pattern: Set tasks as bullets and end on the strongest question.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the tasks into one paragraph.

units.rhetorical_move: says some assumptions may be relaxed

original_instantiations: quantification needs simpler assumptions
some of them may be relaxed

units.source_excerpt: In order to better quantify the model, we may relax some of the assumptions.
units.reusable_pattern: Preface a list of assumptions with we may relax.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat every assumption as fixed.

units.rhetorical_move: says consumers pursue maximum utility

original_instantiations: consumers are called rational
they pursue maximum utility

units.source_excerpt: Consumers are rational and pursue maximum utility.
units.reusable_pattern: State rationality and the objective in one sentence.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a second objective.

units.rhetorical_move: says the government aims at four things

original_instantiations: the government has four aims
growth, employment, price stability and equilibrium

units.source_excerpt: The government aims at growth, employment, price stability and equilibrium.
units.reusable_pattern: Count a government's aims instead of naming one.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop one of the four.

units.rhetorical_move: points at the parameter table

original_instantiations: the parameters are listed in a table
the table is written as Tabel

units.source_excerpt: The parameters are listed in a table whose caption is misspelled.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the misspelled table caption.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the caption when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: splits the world into two paths
units.function: refuse one path, then take the other

original_instantiations: one path has every central bank refusing the currency
the other has not all of them refusing

units.source_excerpt: One path has every bank refusing, and the other has not all of them refusing.
units.reusable_pattern: Split a choice into two paths and take the second.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not analyze both paths equally.

units.rhetorical_move: says the currency will directly enter the model
units.function: close the path with a consequence

original_instantiations: a bank of influence treats the currency as traditional
the currency then enters the open model directly

units.source_excerpt: From the analysis above, the currency will directly enter the existing model.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a path with from the analysis above.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the path without its consequence.

units.rhetorical_move: builds a virtual country and a mysterious organization

original_instantiations: a mysterious organization issues the currency
a virtual country is envisioned around it

units.source_excerpt: We assume a mysterious organization issues the currency, and we envision a virtual country.
units.reusable_pattern: Invent an issuer with we assume and we envision.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the country as real.

units.rhetorical_move: says each unit can be infinitely divided

original_instantiations: the total amount issued is a constant
each unit can be infinitely divided

units.source_excerpt: The total issued is a constant, and each unit can be infinitely divided.
units.reusable_pattern: Pair a fixed total with infinite divisibility.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop either property.

units.rhetorical_move: defines demand as what the public is willing to hold

original_instantiations: demand is the amount the public is willing to hold
the public weighs benefits against costs

units.source_excerpt: Demand is the amount the public is willing to hold after weighing benefits and costs.
units.reusable_pattern: Define demand through willingness and a weighing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define demand as a stock alone.

units.rhetorical_move: lists three motives

original_instantiations: three motives are listed
transactions, precautionary and speculative

units.source_excerpt: Demand is set by three motives: transactions, precautionary and speculative.
units.reusable_pattern: List motives in the textbook order.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reorder them.

units.rhetorical_move: interprets currency as treasure retained

original_instantiations: currency is read as treasure people retain
income is held invariant

units.source_excerpt: Currency is interpreted as the treasure people are willing to retain.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the treasure metaphor.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten treasure to money.

units.rhetorical_move: reads points off the curve

original_instantiations: points above the curve mean insufficient demand
points below mean excessive demand

units.source_excerpt: Points above the curve mean insufficient demand, and points below mean excessive demand.
units.reusable_pattern: Read both sides of a curve.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read only one side.

units.rhetorical_move: says higher sensitivity makes the curve flatter

original_instantiations: sensitivity to interest rates rises
the curve grows flatter

units.source_excerpt: The higher the sensitivity to interest rates, the flatter the curve.
units.reusable_pattern: Tie a slope to a sensitivity with the higher, the flatter.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reverse the direction.

units.rhetorical_move: says the curve describes all possible combinations
units.function: define a curve by its pairs

original_instantiations: the curve pairs interest rate with real output
other factors are held given

units.source_excerpt: The curve describes all possible combinations of interest rate and real output.
units.reusable_pattern: Define a curve as all possible combinations.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name a single point.

units.rhetorical_move: says the buying price equals the selling price

original_instantiations: no exchange control is assumed
the buying price equals the selling price

units.source_excerpt: There is no exchange control, and the buying price equals the selling price.
units.reusable_pattern: Remove the spread in one clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a spread.

units.rhetorical_move: says the change is several times the intervention

original_instantiations: the bank buys the new currency and sells its own
the money supply changes by several times the intervention

units.source_excerpt: The change in the money supply is several times the official intervention.
units.reusable_pattern: Magnify an intervention with several times.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the change equals the intervention.

units.rhetorical_move: says people will frantically want to exchange

original_instantiations: a war is the example
holders frantically want to exchange and move the money

units.source_excerpt: Holders will frantically want to exchange the currency and move the money.
units.reusable_pattern: Dramatize an outflow with frantically.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the adverb.

units.rhetorical_move: states the rule as that is to say

original_instantiations: instruments must at least equal objectives
the restatement says one goal needs one tool

units.source_excerpt: That is to say, one economic goal needs at least one independent tool.
units.reusable_pattern: Restate a rule with that is to say.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the restatement.

units.rhetorical_move: says the floating rate realizes equilibrium spontaneously

original_instantiations: the rate floats freely
external equilibrium arrives spontaneously

units.source_excerpt: The floating rate realizes external equilibrium spontaneously.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit a mechanism with spontaneously.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add an intervention.

units.rhetorical_move: gives the conclusion from the figure

original_instantiations: the figure and a second figure are read together
the conclusion names inflation and a deficit

units.source_excerpt: From the figure we can give the conclusion that inflation and a deficit both hold.
units.reusable_pattern: Draw a policy from a figure with we can give the conclusion.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not state the policy before the figure.

units.rhetorical_move: says the country finally achieves equilibrium

original_instantiations: the policy is tight and the curve moves left
equilibrium is finally achieved

units.source_excerpt: The policy is tight, the curve moves left, and equilibrium is finally achieved.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the lowercase opening of the last clause.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not capitalize the clause when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: asks whether the test is viable and reliable

original_instantiations: an anova test is applied
the question is whether it is viable and reliable

units.source_excerpt: The test is applied to see whether it is viable and reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: Judge a test by viable and reliable together.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not keep only one of the two.

units.rhetorical_move: says each variable is indispensable

original_instantiations: the coefficients are both small
each variable is called indispensable

units.source_excerpt: Each variable is indispensable, and the coefficients are both small.
units.reusable_pattern: Read small coefficients as evidence that nothing can be dropped.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a small coefficient unimportant.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model is insensitive to outliers

original_instantiations: the model does not change significantly when variables fluctuate
it is called insensitive to outliers

units.source_excerpt: It is reasonable to consider the model insensitive to outliers.
units.reusable_pattern: Close a sensitivity test with it is reasonable to consider.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the model never changes.

units.rhetorical_move: says the result attests to the effectiveness

original_instantiations: the model is applied to two further countries
the result attests to the effectiveness

units.source_excerpt: A second country attests to the effectiveness of the model.
units.reusable_pattern: Confirm a model with attests to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat one country as enough.

units.rhetorical_move: says the models are significant enough

original_instantiations: the same test is run in R
the models are called significant enough to explain the cases

units.source_excerpt: Using the test in R, the models are significant enough to explain the cases.
units.reusable_pattern: Borrow a tool with using, then claim enough.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the models explain every case.

units.rhetorical_move: says the ideas are proposed creatively

original_instantiations: the framework runs from the individual to the macro level
the ideas are called creative

units.source_excerpt: We creatively propose ideas and models for the new currency.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim novelty with creatively.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the adverb.

units.rhetorical_move: says the equations fail to truly portray

original_instantiations: the equations are linear
they fail to truly portray some countries

units.source_excerpt: The equations are linear and fail to truly portray some countries.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit a limit with fail to truly portray.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the failure.

units.rhetorical_move: says only two countries are considered

original_instantiations: the interaction studied covers two countries only
the wider set is left out

units.source_excerpt: We only consider the interaction between two countries.
units.reusable_pattern: State a narrow scope with we only consider.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not imply the rest was checked.

units.rhetorical_move: repeats the abstract's finding

original_instantiations: the representative model is built first
the same finding about either system is repeated

units.source_excerpt: The closing repeats the finding that either system reaches equilibrium under proper policies.
units.reusable_pattern: Close by repeating the abstract's finding.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce a new result in the close.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers sources in brackets

original_instantiations: each source opens with a bracketed number
several entries are duplicated

units.source_excerpt: Sources open with a bracketed number, and some entries repeat.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the bracketed numbering.
prohibited_generalizations: The citation list belongs to this paper and does not transfer.
